name: comet-dial
title: Comet Dial
description: A circular control open at the bottom, showing a large number inside and a coloured arc from the start to the current value. Dragging or flicking the arc changes the value with a springy overshoot, and a comet tail trails the moving handle.
use: A dashboard or media control wants a compact, tactile dial instead of a straight slider.
avoid: It is a fixed square size with a large dead centre, and small drags make precise values fiddly.
a11y: Full keyboard control and a proper slider role, but the dial draws no focus ring when tabbed to. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: Two open-ring dials side by side on black, each with a faint full arc and a bright coloured arc ending in a small round handle. A large light number sits in the middle with a smaller unit, and the rings are open at the bottom.
behaves: Dragging around the arc follows the pointer, and releasing with speed flicks the value on and springs it back with a small overshoot at the ends. A widening comet tail streaks behind the handle while it moves, and keys step the value.
customise: Props set the value, range, step, unit, label, accent and ink colours, size, sweep, thickness, speed, bounce, momentum and comet reach and width.
weight: light: One SVG arc and a dozen comet segments, animated only while the value moves.
demo: Two dials, Volume at 62 percent and Temperature at 21 degrees, with Volume changing during the clip.
issues: There is no visible focus indicator on the dial.
polishWhy: Distinctive comet motion and a clean big readout; the thin track is low contrast at rest.
